raw_record.question_text:
The rectangular coil has $N=100$ turns, $ab=30\,\mathrm{cm}$, $ad=20\,\mathrm{cm}$, and the magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $B=1.0\,\mathrm{T}$. It starts to rotate uniformly from the position shown in the diagram around the axis $OO'$ with an angular velocity of $\omega=100\,\mathrm{rad/s}$.

1. Find the maximum induced electromotive force $E_m$ generated by the coil.
2. Write the expression for the induced electromotive force $e$ as a function of time.

method.method_draft: Use the magnetic-flux form of Faraday's law. From the image, read that the rectangular coil abcd is initially drawn in the plane of the page, the uniform magnetic field arrows point horizontally from left to right in the same plane as the coil, and the rotation axis OO' is the vertical dashed line through the coil. From the text, read N=100, ab=30 cm, ad=20 cm, B=1.0 T, and angular speed ω=100 rad/s. Convert the side lengths to meters and compute the coil area S=ab·ad=0.30·0.20=0.060 m^2. Since the image shows the field initially lying in the plane of the coil, the initial magnetic flux is zero and the flux can be written as Φ=NBS sin(ωt) up to sign convention. Apply e=-dΦ/dt, giving an emf proportional to cos(ωt), with amplitude Em=NBSω=100·1.0·0.060·100=600 V. Choose the sign convention consistent with the standard positive direction to write e=600 cos(100t) V.

method.method_draft: Use the motional-emf contribution of the moving sides instead of starting from flux. From the image, identify OO' as the central vertical rotation axis, ab as the horizontal width of the coil, ad as the vertical height, and the magnetic field as horizontal. When the coil rotates about the vertical axis, the two vertical sides ad and bc move through the magnetic field and act as the active conductors; the horizontal sides do not contribute to the line integral in this geometry. From the text, take ab=0.30 m, ad=0.20 m, B=1.0 T, N=100, and ω=100 rad/s. At an angle θ=ωt from the shown position, the horizontal distance of each active vertical side from the axis projected perpendicular to the field gives an effective speed contribution proportional to (ab/2)ω cosθ. The two vertical sides add, so the emf per turn is B·ad·ω·ab·cosθ=B(ab·ad)ω cos(ωt). Multiplying by N gives e=NBab·ad·ω cos(ωt)=600 cos(100t) V, so the maximum value is 600 V.
